title: The return of monkey life
description: 完整答案表、全文段落速覽，以及逐題 Skim、Scan、Read、同義改寫與中伏位分析。

questions.prompt: A reason why newer forests provide howlers with better feeding opportunities than older forests
questions.translation: 為何較新的森林比舊森林能給 howlers 更好的覓食機會。

blocks.text: “Howlers persist at La Pacifica, Glander explains, because they are leaf-eaters.”
Glander 解釋，howlers 能在 La Pacifica 持續生存，是因為牠們是吃葉子的猴類。
“In younger forests, trees put most of their limited energy into growing wood, leaves, and fruit, so they produce much lower levels of toxin than do well-established, old-growth trees.”
在較年輕的森林中，樹木會把有限能量大多用於生長木質、葉子和果實，所以牠們產生的 toxin水平比成熟的 old-growth trees 低得多。
只看首尾句，Paragraph C 明顯處理 howlers 的飲食和 newer forests 的優勢。題目問 newer forests 為何 feeding opportunities 較好；尾句直接比較 younger forests 和 old-growth trees。
掃描 Paragraph C 時，中後段直接出現 “regenerating forests” 和 “younger forests”，這些都是newer forests 的同義表達。
“The leaves that grow in regenerating forests, like those at La Pacifica, are actually more howler-friendly than those produced by the centuries-old trees that survive farther south.”
像 La Pacifica 這類再生森林中生長的葉子，其實比南方那些數百年老樹產生的葉子更適合howlers。
“In younger forests, trees put most of their limited energy into growing wood, leaves, and fruit, so they produce much lower levels of toxin than do well-established, old-growth trees.”
在年輕森林中，樹木大多把有限能量用於長木質、葉和果實，所以毒素水平比成熟老樹低得多。
題目中的 “newer forests” 對應 “regenerating forests / younger forests”；“older forests” 對應
“centuries-old trees / old-growth trees”；“better feeding opportunities” 對應 “more howler-friendly”
。真正原因是：年輕樹木毒素較少，howlers 吃葉時負擔較低。

questions.prompt: A reference to a change in farmers’ attitudes towards wildlife
questions.translation: 提到 farmers 對 wildlife 的態度改變。

blocks.text: “Estrada believes the monkeys bring underappreciated benefits to such plantations, dispersing the seeds of figs and other shade trees, and fertilizing the soil.”
Estrada 認為，monkeys 為這類 plantation 帶來被低估的好處，包括傳播 figs 和其他 shade trees 的種子，以及令土壤更肥沃。

“‘Conservation is usually viewed as a conflict between farming practices and the need to preserve nature,’ Estrada says. ‘We’re moving away from that vision and beginning to consider ways in which commercial activities may become a tool for the conservation of primates in human-modified landscapes.’”

Estrada 說：「保育通常被視為 farming practices 和 preserve nature 之間的衝突。我們正離開這種看法，開始思考 commercial activities 如何在 human-modified landscapes 中成為 primates conservation 的工具。」首句講 monkeys 對 plantations 有益，尾句講人們開始改變 conservation vs farming 的想法。這正好對應 farmers’ attitudes towards wildlife 的改變。
原文沒有直接說 “attitudes changed”，但有幾個強訊號：
“farmers will begin to see the advantages”
“commercial activities may become a tool for the conservation of primates”
“begin to see” 和 “moving away” 都表示觀念轉變。
關鍵原文：“He hopes that farmers will begin to see the advantages of associating with wild monkeys, which could include potential ecotourism projects.”
他希望 farmers 會開始看到與 wild monkeys 共存的好處，其中可能包括 ecotourism projects。
這句直接對應題目。題目說 “a change in farmers’ attitudes”，原文用 “will begin to see the advantages”。也就是說，farmers 原本可能把 wildlife 視為麻煩或衝突來源，但 Estrada 希望他們開始看到 wild monkeys 的好處。
“that vision” 指前一句所說 conservation 和 farming practices 互相衝突的看法。整段真正想突出的是：農業和野生 primates 可以互相配合。所以 29 答案是 G。

questions.prompt: A description of the means by which howlers select the best available diet for themselves
questions.translation: 描述 howlers 用甚麼方法為自己選出最佳可用食物。

blocks.text: “Howlers persist at La Pacifica, Glander explains, because they are leaf-eaters.”
Glander 解釋，howlers 能在 La Pacifica 持續生存，是因為牠們是吃葉子的猴類。
“In younger forests, trees put most of their limited energy into growing wood, leaves, and fruit, so they produce much lower levels of toxin than do well-established, old-growth trees.”
在較年輕森林中，樹木大多把有限能量放在生長木質、葉子和果實上，所以毒素水平比 mature old-growth trees 低得多。
Paragraph C 的段落功能是解釋 howlers 的飲食適應能力，包括吃葉、處理 toxins，以及選擇nutritious food items。題目問 “select the best available diet”，自然應在這段尋找。
掃描時要留意 select 不一定原字重現，可能用 “sampling” 和 “focusing” 表示選擇過程。

“Watching generations of howlers at La Pacifica has shown Glander that the monkeys keep their systems primed by sampling a variety of plants and then focusing on a small number of the most nutritious food items.”
Glander 觀察 La Pacifica 幾代 howlers 後發現，這些猴子會先試食多種植物，讓身體系統保持準備狀態，然後集中進食少數最有營養的食物。
這句完整描述 “means”。方法分兩步：先 “sampling a variety of plants”：試食多種植物。
再 “focusing on a small number of the most nutritious food items”：集中在少數最有營養的食物上。
題目中的 “select the best available diet” 就是這句的概括。howlers 不是隨機吃葉，而是透過sampling 和 focusing 找到更有營養、較合適的食物。

questions.prompt: Figures relating to the reduction of natural wildlife habitat over a period of time
questions.translation: 關於自然 wildlife habitat 隨時間減少的數字。

blocks.text: “Ken Glander, a primatologist from Duke University in the USA, is studying La Pacifica’s monkeys in an effort to understand the relationship between howlers and regenerating forests at the edges of grazing lands.”
美國 Duke University 的 primatologist Ken Glander 正研究 La Pacifica 的 monkeys，以了解howlers 和 grazing lands 邊緣 regenerating forests 的關係。
“In the 18th century, tropical dry forests once covered most of Central America, but by the 1980s less than two percent remained undisturbed, and less than one percent was protected.”
在 18 世紀，tropical dry forests 曾覆蓋 Central America 大部分地區，但到 1980s，少於 2% 保持未受干擾，少於 1% 受到保護。
只看尾句已經可見 habitat reduction 的 figures：18th century、1980s、less than two percent、less than one percent。
這些數字和時間跨度非常明顯，定位到 Paragraph B 最後一句。
“In the 18th century, tropical dry forests once covered most of Central America, but by the 1980s less than two percent remained undisturbed, and less than one percent was protected.”
在 18 世紀，熱帶乾林曾覆蓋 Central America 大部分地方，但到了 1980s，保持未受干擾的少於2%，受保護的少於 1%。

題目中的 “natural wildlife habitat” 對應 “tropical dry forests”。這類森林是當地 primates 的自然棲息地。題目中的 “reduction over a period of time” 對應從 “18th century” 到 “1980s” 的變化。原文由 “covered most of Central America” 變成 “less than two percent remained undisturbed”，明顯是大幅減少。

questions.prompt: Howler monkeys have a more rapid rate of 32 ______ than either capuchin or spider monkeys.
questions.translation: Howler monkeys 的 ______ 速度比 capuchin 或 spider monkeys 更快。

blocks.text: “Some of the same traits that allow howlers to survive at La Pacifica also explain their population boom in Santa Rosa.”
一些讓 howlers 能在 La Pacifica 生存的特徵，也解釋了牠們在 Santa Rosa 的 population boom。
“This ability gives them a real advantage over capuchin and spider monkeys, which have suffered during the long, ongoing drought in the area.”
這種能力讓牠們比 capuchin 和 spider monkeys 更有優勢；後兩者在該地長期持續的 drought 中受苦。
這段是 howlers advantages 的集中段。題目 summary 標題也是 “Why do howlers have an advantage…”，所以 Paragraph E 是主段落。
“Howler reproduction is faster than that of other native monkey species.”
題目中的 “more rapid rate of ___” 需要一個名詞。原文直接給出名詞 “reproduction”。
“Howler reproduction is faster than that of other native monkey species.”
Howlers 的繁殖比其他本地猴類更快。
“They give birth for the first time at about 3.5 years of age, compared with seven years for capuchins, and eight or more for spider monkeys.”
牠們大約 3.5 歲首次生育，相比之下，capuchins 是 7 歲，spider monkeys 是 8 歲或以上。
題目 “a more rapid rate of” 後面應填名詞。原文 “reproduction is faster” 改寫成 “more rapid rate of reproduction”。答案只需一個詞，符合 ONE WORD ONLY。

questions.prompt: Unlike the other local monkey species, howlers can survive without eating 33 ______ and so can live inside a relatively small habitat area.
questions.translation: 不同於其他本地猴類，howlers 即使不吃 ______ 也能生存，所以可生活在較小棲息範圍內。

blocks.text: “Howlers persist at La Pacifica, Glander explains, because they are leaf-eaters.”
Glander 解釋，howlers 能在 La Pacifica 持續存在，是因為牠們是吃葉子的猴類。
“In younger forests, trees put most of their limited energy into growing wood, leaves, and fruit, so they produce much lower levels of toxin than do well-established, old-growth trees.”
在年輕森林中，樹木把大部分有限能量用於長木質、葉子和果實，所以毒素水平比成熟老樹低得多。
題目問 howlers 和其他 monkey species 的飲食差異。Paragraph C 首句已經說 howlers 是leaf-eaters，因此可以推測答案和 fruit 依賴程度有關。
“They eat fruit when it is available but, unlike capuchin and spider monkeys, do not depend on large areas of fruiting trees.”
題目中的 “without eating ___” 對應原文 “do not depend on large areas of fruiting trees”。空格前是 eating，答案需填食物名詞。
“They eat fruit when it is available but, unlike capuchin and spider monkeys, do not depend on large areas of fruiting trees.”
有 fruit 時牠們會吃，但不同於 capuchin 和 spider monkeys，牠們不依賴大片結出果實的樹林。
題目把這句改寫成 “can survive without eating fruit”。原文沒有說 howlers 完全不吃 fruit；它說有fruit 時會吃，但不依賴 large areas of fruiting trees。這足以支持 summary 的意思：howlers 可以在缺少大量 fruiting trees 的較小棲息地中生存。
答案只能填一個詞，所以不可填 “fruiting trees”。空格前是 “eating”，最自然、最符合原文的食物名詞是 fruit。

questions.prompt: Their diet is more flexible, and they are able to tolerate leaves with high levels of 34______.
questions.translation: 牠們的飲食更靈活，也能忍受含有高水平 ______ 的葉子。

blocks.text: “Howlers persist at La Pacifica, Glander explains, because they are leaf-eaters.”
Glander 解釋，howlers 能在 La Pacifica 留存，是因為牠們是 leaf-eaters。
“In younger forests, trees put most of their limited energy into growing wood, leaves, and fruit, so they produce much lower levels of toxin than do well-established, old-growth trees.”
在較年輕森林中，樹木大多把有限能量用於長木質、葉子和果實，所以產生的 toxin 水平比成熟老樹低得多。
Paragraph C 全段圍繞 howlers 的 leaf diet 和 toxins。題目有 “leaves with high levels of”，自然定位到 “toxins”。
“ability to thrive on leaves loaded with toxins”
“long-term exposure to a specific plant toxin”
“loaded with toxins” 就是 “high levels of toxins”。
關鍵原文：“Glander is particularly interested in howlers’ ability to thrive on leaves loaded with toxins—poisonous substances designed to protect the plants.”
Glander 特別感興趣的是 howlers 能靠含有 toxins 的葉子 thrive；這些 toxins 是植物用來保護自己的有毒物質。
題目中的 “tolerate leaves with high levels of” 是原文 “thrive on leaves loaded with toxins” 的改寫。
“loaded with” 表示含量很多；“toxins” 是有毒物質。原文還用 “poisonous substances” 解釋 toxins，進一步確認答案。答案要 ONE WORD ONLY，填複數 toxins，因為原文用 plural。所以 34 答案是 toxins。

questions.prompt: Howlers can also survive periods of 35 ______ better than the other monkey species can.
questions.translation: Howlers 也比其他猴類更能熬過 ______ 時期。

blocks.text: “Some of the same traits that allow howlers to survive at La Pacifica also explain their population boom in Santa Rosa.”
一些讓 howlers 在 La Pacifica 存活的特徵，也解釋了牠們在 Santa Rosa 的族群大增。
“This ability gives them a real advantage over capuchin and spider monkeys, which have suffered during the long, ongoing drought in the area.”
這種能力讓牠們比 capuchin 和 spider monkeys 更有優勢；後兩者在該區長期持續的 drought 中受苦。
題目問 “survive periods of ___ better”。Paragraph E 最後一句直接提到 long, ongoing drought，並比較 howlers 和其他猴類。
“survive away from open streams and water holes”
“real advantage over capuchin and spider monkeys”
空格前是 “periods of”，後面應該填一個抽象或環境狀態名詞。原文中符合的是 drought。
“Also crucial is the fact that the leaves howlers eat hold plenty of water, so the monkeys can survive away from open streams and water holes.”
同樣關鍵的是，howlers 所吃的葉子含有大量水分，所以牠們即使遠離開放溪流和水洞也能生存。
“This ability gives them a real advantage over capuchin and spider monkeys, which have suffered during the long, ongoing drought in the area.”
這種能力讓牠們比 capuchin 和 spider monkeys 更有優勢；後兩者在該區長期持續的乾旱中受苦。
題目中的 “survive periods of drought better” 是把兩句合併：葉子含水 → howlers 可遠離水源生存 → 在 drought 中比其他猴類更有優勢。
答案只需一個詞，原文詞是 drought。

questions.prompt: It has seen the return of native tree species.
questions.translation: 這個地點見證了 native tree species 的回歸。

blocks.text: “The value of maturing forests to primates is also a subject of study at Santa Rosa National Park, about 35 miles northwest of La Pacifica.”
成熟中的森林對 primates 的價值，也是 Santa Rosa National Park 的研究主題；該地位於 La Pacifica 西北約 35 miles。
“In the first 28 years following protection of the area, the capuchin population doubled, while the number of howlers increased sevenfold.”
在該區受保護後的頭 28 年，capuchin population 翻倍，howlers 數量增加七倍。
首句直接定位 Santa Rosa National Park，段落中間講 burned forest、government protection、indigenous trees returning。題目問 native tree species return，目標段落很明確。
“indigenous” = native；“had been absent” + “began to invade” 表示回歸。
關鍵原文：“But in 1971 the government protected the area by designating it a National Park, and species of indigenous trees which had been absent for decades began to invade the abandoned pastures.”
但在 1971 年，政府把該區指定為 National Park 加以保護；已消失數十年的 indigenous trees 開始進入 abandoned pastures。
題目中的 “return of native tree species” 對應 “species of indigenous trees which had been absent for decades began to invade”。地點是 Santa Rosa National Park。

questions.prompt: It supports only one species of native monkey.
questions.translation: 這個地點只支持一種 native monkey。

blocks.text: “Hacienda La Pacifica, a remote working cattle ranch in Guanacaste province of northern Costa Rica, has for decades been home to a community of mantled howler monkeys.”
Hacienda La Pacifica 是 Costa Rica 北部 Guanacaste province 一個偏遠的運作中 cattle ranch，幾十年來一直是一群 mantled howler monkeys 的家。
“In the process, the farmer unwittingly founded a unique laboratory for the study of monkeys.”
在這個過程中，這位 farmer 無意間建立了一個研究 monkeys 的獨特實驗室。
Paragraph A 首句說 La Pacifica 現在有 mantled howler monkeys；接下來說其他 native primates曾經 common，但後來 vanished。這正好對應 “only one species”。
“Other native primates … were once common … but vanished”
“vanished” 是關鍵，說明其他 native primates 現在不在該區。
關鍵原文：“Hacienda La Pacifica … has for decades been home to a community of mantled howler monkeys.”
Hacienda La Pacifica 幾十年來一直是一群 mantled howler monkeys 的家。

“Other native primates—white-faced capuchin monkeys and spider monkeys—were once common in this area, too, but vanished after the Pan-American Highway was built nearby in the 1950s and most of the surrounding land was cleared for cattle-raising.”
其他 native primates，包括 white-faced capuchin monkeys 和 spider monkeys，曾經在此區也很常見，但在 1950s 附近建成 Pan-American Highway、周圍大多土地被清理作 cattle-raising 後消失了。
這兩句合起來表示：La Pacifica 目前保留的 native monkey community 是 mantled howlers；其他兩種曾經存在，但已 vanished。題目中的 “supports only one species” 對應這種現況。

questions.prompt: Its monkey population helps the agriculture of the area.
questions.translation: 這個地點的 monkey population 幫助當地農業。

blocks.text: “Estrada believes the monkeys bring underappreciated benefits to such plantations, dispersing the seeds of figs and other shade trees, and fertilizing the soil.”
Estrada 認為，monkeys 為這類 plantations 帶來被低估的好處，包括傳播 figs 和其他 shade trees 的種子，以及令土壤更肥沃。

“‘Conservation is usually viewed as a conflict between farming practices and the need to preserve nature,’ Estrada says. ‘We’re moving away from that vision and beginning to consider ways in which commercial activities may become a tool for the conservation of primates in human-modified landscapes.’”
Estrada 說，保育通常被視為 farming practices 和 preserve nature 的衝突；現在人們開始思考commercial activities 如何成為 human-modified landscapes 中的 primate conservation 工具。
Paragraph G 直接講 plantations 和 monkeys 的 benefits。上一段 F 的地點是 Cholula Cacao Farm，所以答案應是 C。
“plantations” 和 “cacao pods” 都屬於 agriculture。
關鍵原文：“Estrada believes the monkeys bring underappreciated benefits to such plantations, dispersing the seeds of figs and other shade trees, and fertilizing the soil.”
Estrada 認為，這些 monkeys 為 plantations 帶來被低估的好處：牠們傳播 figs 和其他 shade trees 的種子，也令土壤更肥沃。
“The howlers eat the leaves and fruit of the shade trees, leaving the valuable cacao pods alone.”
Howlers 吃 shade trees 的葉子和果實，並留下有價值的 cacao pods，不會吃掉它們。
地點是 Cholula Cacao Farm。Monkeys 幫助農業有兩層：第一，牠們不破壞 cacao pods；第二，牠們幫助 shade trees 散播種子和肥沃土壤，這些 shade trees 又保護 cacao crop。

questions.prompt: It is home to populations of all three local monkey species.
questions.translation: 這個地點是三種本地猴類族群的家。

blocks.text: “The value of maturing forests to primates is also a subject of study at Santa Rosa National Park, about 35 miles northwest of La Pacifica.”
成熟中的森林對 primates 的價值，也在 Santa Rosa National Park 被研究；該地位於 La Pacifica西北約 35 miles。
“In the first 28 years following protection of the area, the capuchin population doubled, while the number of howlers increased sevenfold.”
保護該區後的頭 28 年，capuchin population 翻倍，howlers 數量增加七倍。
Paragraph D 會講 Santa Rosa 的 forest recovery 和 monkey return。題目說 all three local monkey species，要找 capuchins、howlers、spider monkeys 同時出現的位置。
掃描 Paragraph D 可以找到三者按順序回到 reborn forests。
“Capuchins were the first to begin using the reborn forests, followed by howlers.”
Capuchins 是第一批開始使用重生森林的猴類，之後是 howlers。
“Eventually, even spider monkeys, fruit-eaters that need large areas of continuous forest, returned.”
最後，甚至需要大片連續森林的 fruit-eating spider monkeys 也回來了。
這兩句列出三種猴類：capuchins、howlers、spider monkeys。地點是 Santa Rosa National Park。
題目中的 “home to populations of all three” 對應這個回歸過程。

questions.prompt: Its landscape was altered by the construction of a transport link.
questions.translation: 這個地點的景觀因交通連接的建設而改變。

blocks.text: “Hacienda La Pacifica, a remote working cattle ranch in Guanacaste province of northern Costa Rica, has for decades been home to a community of mantled howler monkeys.”
Hacienda La Pacifica 是 Costa Rica 北部 Guanacaste province 一個偏遠 cattle ranch，幾十年來一直是一群 mantled howler monkeys 的家。
“In the process, the farmer unwittingly founded a unique laboratory for the study of monkeys.”
在此過程中，這位 farmer 無意間建立了一個研究 monkeys 的獨特實驗室。
Paragraph A 介紹 Hacienda La Pacifica 的地理和土地變化背景。題目中的 “transport link” 不會原字出現，應找 highway / road 之類詞。
“most of the surrounding land was cleared for cattle-raising”
“Highway” 是 transport link；“was built” 對應 construction；“land was cleared” 對應 landscape altered。

關鍵原文：“Other native primates—white-faced capuchin monkeys and spider monkeys—were once common in this area, too, but vanished after the Pan-American Highway was built nearby in the 1950s and most of the surrounding land was cleared for cattle-raising.”
其他 native primates，包括 white-faced capuchin monkeys 和 spider monkeys，曾經在此區也很常見，但在 1950s 附近建成 Pan-American Highway、周圍大多土地被清理作 cattle-raising 後消失了。
題目中的 “transport link” 指 “Pan-American Highway”。景觀改變有兩部分：highway built nearby，以及 surrounding land cleared for cattle-raising。這段位置是 Hacienda La Pacifica，所以location 是 A。

paragraphOverview.title: 全文 Skim Roadmap
paragraphOverview.intro: 先掌握每段的功能與主旨，再進入逐題定位和細讀分析。

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph A 首句介紹 Hacienda La Pacifica，說這個 Costa Rica 北部的 cattle ranch 幾十年來一直有 mantled howler monkeys。尾句說 ranch owner 保留 native trees 的做法，無意中建立了一個研究 monkeys 的獨特實驗室。只看首尾句，可以先估計這段會交代地點背景、原有猴類變化，以及農場樹帶如何讓 howlers 留下來。段落功能偏向介紹研究場景。

Paragraph B 首句引入 Duke University 的 Ken Glander，說他研究 La Pacifica 的 monkeys，以理解 howlers 和 grazing lands 邊緣再生森林的關係。尾句給出 tropical dry forests 的驚人減少數字：到 1980s，少於 2% 未受干擾，少於 1% 受保護。只看首尾句，這段重點是研究價值和棲息地消失背景，特別適合處理 habitat reduction 題。
Paragraph C 首句說 howlers 能在 La Pacifica 持續存在，原因是牠們是 leaf-eaters。尾句比較younger forests 和 old-growth trees，指出年輕森林樹木產生的 toxin 水平較低。只看首尾句，可以推測這段會解釋 howlers 的飲食優勢：牠們不太依賴大量果樹，能吃葉，也能處理植物毒素；年輕再生林對牠們特別有利。

Paragraph D 首句把研究場景轉到 Santa Rosa National Park，說 maturing forests 對 primates的價值也在那裡被研究。尾句給出保護後 28 年的猴群增長數字：capuchin population doubled， howlers increased sevenfold。只看首尾句，這段會講被破壞森林在保護後重新恢復，native trees和不同猴類回歸，重點是 habitat regeneration 及其效果。

Paragraph E 首句說 howlers 在 La Pacifica 能生存的特徵，也解釋了牠們在 Santa Rosa 的population boom。尾句說 howlers 因能從 leaves 攝取大量水分，在 ongoing drought 中比capuchins 和 spider monkeys 更有優勢。只看首尾句，這段功能很清楚：比較 howlers 和其他猴類，解釋牠們在人類改變環境中的生存優勢。

Paragraph F 首句介紹 Alejandro Estrada 研究一群生活在人類完全改變棲息地中的 howler monkeys，地點是 Mexico Tabasco 的 cacao plantation。尾句說 howlers 吃 shade trees 的leaves and fruit，留下 valuable cacao pods。只看首尾句，這段重點是 Cholula Cacao Farm： cacao 需要 shade trees，人類種樹後 howlers 遷入，形成農業和野生猴群共存的案例。

Paragraph G 首句說 Estrada 認為 monkeys 為 plantations 帶來被低估的好處，包括 dispersing seeds 和 fertilizing soil。尾句引用 Estrada，指出 conservation 不必總被看作 farming practices和 preserve nature 的衝突，commercial activities 也可能成為 primate conservation 的工具。只看首尾句，這段是全文收束：農民態度、猴子益處、生態旅遊、農業與保育共存。
